source_contact.full_declaration_inventory: All three embedded module blocks in the published text were indexed for definitions, imports, data nodes, features and notifications. An index entry alone gives no semantic correspondence.
selected_meanings_read: Sections 2 and 3.1: scope and component key/class.
Section 7.1 /hardware/component: detection and intended-configuration matching by class, parent and parent-relative position, including fallback when no entry matches.
Section 7.1 /hardware/component/mfg-name: manufacturer context for comparing serial, model, firmware and software revision.
Appendix A: the legacy state-only representation has a different standing.
source_contact.companion_routing: Sections 4, 5 and 6 supply in-RFC mappings to ENTITY-MIB, ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB and ENTITY-STATE-MIB. These do not imply independent semantic review of every object in the referenced MIBs.
source_contact.current_review: Verified original text fingerprint. Compared the principal schema and its descriptions, initial class identities, §§3–6 and Appendix A standing. Referenced MIB contact limited to listed definitions.

comparison_questions: When may the client identify an expected component as detected, and when does a slot still describe only planned hardware?
Which identifiers refer to a server-local component, a manufacturer-scoped identity or an individual asset?
Which links express physical containment and sibling position?
How should a client display a scaled reading, age, units and validity alongside the component state?

identity.title: Component identification
identity.meaning: name is a server list key; alias can be configured or supplied locally. UUID and asset tag refer to different authorities. Compare vendor strings in manufacturer context. A URI identifies a component without guaranteeing a network endpoint.

containment.title: Containment and detection
containment.meaning: Optional parent identifies one consistent container even for double-width modules. Position is class-family-relative. Intended configuration can supply the operational entry values when all three match fields agree.

states.title: Component state
states.meaning: Feature-gated. Administrative state is configurable; the other state dimensions are reported. A locked component may have unknown oper-state. Local alarms exclude child alarms.

readings.title: Managed sensor reading
readings.meaning: Read-only and conditional on the hardware-sensor feature and sensor class. Read type, scale and precision with each reading. Unavailable and suspected failure differ. The timestamp covers status and/or value acquisition.

changes.title: Inventory and component transitions
changes.meaning: Inventory notification follows list change. Optional enabled/disabled notifications carry a component reference and administrative and alarm context. They do not carry the whole inventory.

holds.RFC8348-Q1: No case endpoint or inventory was observed. Instance identity, optional features, values and installed equipment require server evidence.
holds.RFC8348-Q2: Bounded to the published March 2018 modules. Later IANA additions, vendor identities and extensions require separate source contact.
holds.RFC8348-Q3: The sensor-value prose uses voltsAC, voltsDC and percentRH while the declared enum spellings are volts-AC, volts-DC and percent-RH. Preserve declared spellings and documented interpretation. No wire interoperability test.

S06-R001.label: Manufacturer name
S06-R001.reason: Manufacturer of this physical component. The server omits the name when unknown.

S06-R002.label: Product model designation
S06-R002.reason: Vendor model identifier, preferably the customer-visible part number. Compare within the manufacturer context.

S06-R003.label: Individual hardware serial number
S06-R003.reason: The preferred vendor serial is the one printed on the component. The YANG leaf is read-only even though the corresponding ENTITY-MIB object can be writable. Preserve the source interface when displaying editability.

S06-R004.label: Persistent System identifier
S06-R004.reason: The physical component may have a UUID or identification URI. Its list key is a name scoped to this server. Persistence of the complete described system through change requires other evidence.

ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST.label: Certificate identity and trust context
ISA-A-CERTIFICATE-TRUST.reason: The hardware inventory, its component state, sensor reading and notifications supply no field for Certificate identity and trust context.

S06-R005.label: Described sensing System / arrangement
S06-R005.reason: One management server can describe an arrangement of hardware components with their types and physical containment. The schema can represent a sensor in that arrangement. It supplies no overall sensing purpose.

S06-R006.label: Network-visible participant
S06-R006.reason: The hardware inventory, its component state, sensor reading and notifications supply no field for Network-visible participant.

SAPIENT-F2-FUSION-ROLE.label: Candidate — Hierarchical fusion Node role and aggregated capabilities
SAPIENT-F2-FUSION-ROLE.reason: The hardware inventory, its component state, sensor reading and notifications supply no field for Hierarchical fusion Node role and aggregated capabilities.

S06-R007.label: Physical constituent
S06-R007.reason: Physical containment is explicit. A multipart backplane can have one inventory representation, and a stack may be virtual. Determine the class before treating every list entry as one physical item.

S06-R008.label: Connected external equipment
S06-R008.reason: A containment edge supplies no cable or external equipment association.

S06-R009.label: Hosting platform / station context
S06-R009.reason: The physical container can establish a sensor’s host enclosure. A station role or its geographic context requires additional evidence.

S06-R013.label: Observed / observable property

S06-R014.label: Observer / observing System
S06-R014.reason: A sensor-class component identified by its list key supplies the managed reading. The server that obtained it and any larger observing system have distinct roles.

S06-R015.label: Performed Observation
S06-R015.reason: The leaf holds the latest measurement obtained by the server. Its timestamp may also reflect obtaining the status. No separately identified observation activity or instrument acquisition time is guaranteed.

N4242-RESOLUTION.reason: Decimal precision carries no energy-dependent detector resolution or uncertainty curve.

N4242-EFFICIENCY.reason: Unit type and scale do not define detector efficiency or the denominator used for a photon response curve.

N4242-WINDOWS.reason: Most recent sensor data lack energy-window boundaries, per-window counts and reset totals.
N4242-WINDOWS.label: Gross counts for specified energy windows and counts since reset

N4242-QC.reason: A sensor's availability or reported operational capability does not document the time or result of a calibration inspection.
N4242-QC.label: Inspection time and reported calibration fitness for service

N4242-LINEAGE.reason: Physical containment and the latest scalar sample do not form a measurement derivation graph.
N4242-LINEAGE.label: Measurement grouping and links from derived results to raw readings

N4242-ALGORITHM.reason: Installed component software revision is distinct from the version, settings, result status and execution time of an analysis.

N4242-NUCLIDE.reason: The scoped hardware measurements do not identify nuclides, inferred activity, confidence or detection limits.
N4242-NUCLIDE.label: Nuclide identification, activity and detection limit

N4242-SOURCE.reason: Inventory placement of a component does not convey the position and shielding of an inferred radiation source.
N4242-SOURCE.label: Estimated nuclide source geometry, shielding and position

N4242-PEAK.reason: Generic scalar types define no spectrum-peak energy, width or integrated net counts.
N4242-PEAK.label: Spectral peak energy, width and continuum-subtracted area

N4242-RATES.reason: The published type vocabulary does not distinguish ambient dose equivalent, exposure, count rate or reset-qualified totals.
N4242-RATES.label: Dose, exposure and count rates with distinct accumulation bases

N4242-ALARM.reason: Alarm severity bits apply to the named component, including a detector if represented as the component. These are active-alarm summaries; they do not identify a particular incident, its energy windows, or how it was annunciated.
N4242-ALARM.label: Radiation alarm detector attribution, energy windows and annunciation

N4242-CHAR.reason: A reading has an acquisition timestamp, and a component can summarize active alarms. Neither is an out-of-limits indicator on an arbitrary characteristic, and no characteristic-group flag is defined.
N4242-CHAR.label: Individual characteristic and group out-of-limits indications

N4242-MEDIA.reason: A component identification URI supplies no capture sequence, perspective, identified item or acquisition-time media workflow.
N4242-MEDIA.label: Acquisition context linking measured items and multimedia

RFC8348-MATCH.loss_if_merged: An empty slot or an offline record alone cannot explain why a replacement inherited a configured name.
RFC8348-MATCH.definition: Identify the matching rule used to associate detected hardware with an intended component entry. The principal model uses class, parent and relative position and re-evaluates after intended-list changes. The deprecated appendix describes an additional manufacturer check. Establish which model the source uses before attributing a configured name to a detected item.

RFC8348-REFRESH.loss_if_merged: A report deadline or physical measurement time cannot establish when the server refreshed a cached value.
RFC8348-REFRESH.definition: Record when the management server last acquired sensor status or a value, the time basis used by the source, and the server refresh interval. RFC 8348 uses a date and time. Its mapped Entity Sensor MIB object uses system uptime at acquisition. A zero interval in milliseconds may mean on demand, on change or unknown.

RFC8348-ENCODING.loss_if_merged: Display accuracy or a null flag does not tell a client when a received number is an error code.

RFC8348-CAPACITY.loss_if_merged: Busy can be inherent to the component and must not be presented as a fault or a numeric task limit.

RFC8348-STANDBY.loss_if_merged: Redundancy membership and an enabled flag cannot tell the operator whether initialization is needed for takeover.

RFC8348-STATE-TIME.loss_if_merged: A reset time, event instant or parameter edit has a different subject and cannot explain a fallback timestamp.

RFC8348-INVENTORY.loss_if_merged: A directory-description change or per-component state report cannot identify the inventory-wide refresh signal.

RFC8348-INDEX.loss_if_merged: Matching the same component across management interfaces needs the table key and its scope.

RFC8348-ADMIN-OPER.label: Administrative permission to use a component and its observed operability
RFC8348-ADMIN-OPER.definition: Record administrative restrictions on use separately from actual operability. Admission can be limited to existing uses, and an administratively unlocked component can still be inoperable. Preserve testing or unknown when operability cannot be reported.
RFC8348-ADMIN-OPER.reason: A control request, usage-capacity state or health condition does not identify both the admission policy and observed operability of the same component.

RFC8348-ALARM-SET.label: Concurrent local alarm severities and repair status
RFC8348-ALARM-SET.definition: Preserve simultaneous component-local alarm severity flags and the repair qualification. Unknown reporting capability differs from an active alarm of indeterminate severity. An empty set means no known active alarms and no known repair. Child alarms are excluded.
RFC8348-ALARM-SET.reason: An alert event or rolled-up health score cannot express multiple concurrent local severities or the limits imposed by an ongoing repair.

RFC8348-MGMT-ALIAS.label: Nonvolatile management alias and authority for assigning it
RFC8348-MGMT-ALIAS.definition: Distinguish the management alias from the inventory list key, display name, manufacturer serial and user asset tag. A network manager can specify the alias. When no configured alias exists the server may supply a locally unique operational value.
RFC8348-MGMT-ALIAS.reason: A mutable name or manufacturer identifier alone cannot represent a durable management handle or distinguish manager configuration from server assignment.

RFC8348-READ-STATUS.label: Server ability to acquire a sensor value and suspected sensor failure
RFC8348-READ-STATUS.definition: Record whether the server can obtain a sensor reading, presently cannot obtain one, or believes the sensor is faulty. The reported fault assessment can follow physical failure or unreliable readings.
RFC8348-READ-STATUS.reason: The presence, absence or numeric content of a reading does not distinguish temporary acquisition difficulty from an assessed sensor failure.

RFC8348-ENTRY-SCOPE.label: Physical scope of an equipment inventory entry
RFC8348-ENTRY-SCOPE.definition: Describe whether the entry denotes a discrete item, multiple physical components reported as one entity, or a grouping of chassis that may be virtual. Preserve the source-defined scope when counting equipment or displaying identity.
RFC8348-ENTRY-SCOPE.reason: An aggregate entry need not enumerate constituent identities. Several representations of one item is the reverse cardinality, and a container relationship alone does not identify the granularity of the entry.

examples.finding: Physical containment and a per-sensor reading identify members. They do not select whether a composite reports a capability in its own name or exposes its member as the provider.
The server reports a named value for a sensor component, with fields that identify the measurement units and how to display them.

A transition notification can include the named hardware component’s administrative and alarm states. It does not represent arbitrary detector properties or require comparison with a previous status report.
Administratively allowing use or reporting existing usage does not issue the application command to take a component active.

The YANG field is a date and time. Its mapped MIB object is the agent uptime when status or value was obtained. Distinguish these time bases. The module does not declare the clock synchronization method.

The RFC identifies sensitive writable and readable hardware data and points to externally defined per-user protection of operations and content. It supplies no native access-rule fields or attribute expressions.
Three revision leaves qualify separate aspects of a component. None is defined as a distinct overall device revision.

A device implementing ENTITY-MIB maps the same operational component to a physical table entry. Additional tables relate sensor values and state. The name or serial access rules may differ across representations.

Status distinguishes inability to obtain a reading from a suspected sensor fault. Absence of the optional value and a valid numeric zero are distinguishable. No disable-implies-omit rule or explicit null reading is specified.

For the standards-track module, matching class, parent and relative position selects intended values including name; otherwise detected values apply. The non-normative legacy description adds a manufacturer check and permits an implementation-specific mismatch alarm. Keep these procedures edition- and module-qualified.
A reading has an acquisition timestamp, and a component can summarize active alarms. Neither is an out-of-limits indicator on an arbitrary characteristic, and no characteristic-group flag is defined.

state.meaning: Configurable administrative permission can admit new users, limit service to existing users, or bar use. When an implementation cannot determine operation accurately under a non-unlocked administrative state, it must report unknown. §7.1 explanatory prose uses down although the declared administrative enum has no down member.

An empty set reports no known active local alarm and no repair. Under-repair may affect interpretation of the other flags. Child alarms are excluded. An individual alarm ID, acknowledgment or subtree health is a distinct matter.

management_handle.standing: Configuration-capable alias; default is permitted; MIB mapping optional.
management_handle.meaning: A network manager can assign a nonvolatile component alias; a server can supply a locally unique operational alias if one was not configured. It is independent of a printed serial, editable label, asset tag, list name or MIB index. Retention across reboots and index changes is specified by the companion MIB for manager-written values associated with the same instantiated physical entity; it is not a universal replacement identity.

managed_granularity.meaning: A single represented backplane may be implemented by multiple physical pieces. A stack can be virtual. A component in multiple containers names one stable parent. Known empty containers should be exposed. Position among siblings is qualified by parent and a common base hardware class; implementations may choose different class-specific numbering series. sensor_status.meaning: Status differentiates available value, presently unobtainable value and suspected sensor malfunction, including hard or soft failure.
